messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@veridian.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Capacity lead times & MAP for Dedicated/Private

Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Veridian is keen to move an evaluation into a short MAP that ties to a capacity reservation. A few key asks from our side:

- We need a mutual action plan that maps evaluation milestones to a procurement decision (we're targeting a committed Dedicated deployment, but want Private on-prem options scoped).
- Lead-time transparency: give us concrete lead times for Dedicated/Private (H100/A100 timelines), buffer sizing guidance, and how Redwood handles transit/backfill if hardware slips.
- Acceptance criteria: performance & cost baselines for the final reservation sign-off.

I've attached a short matrix with our usage profiles and rough RPS/latency targets so you can size pools. Our procurement lead (CC'd) will want a clear timeline to feed into the vendor calendar.

Can you draft a MAP that includes an evaluation window, staging acceptance, and a procurement commit milestone? Prefer to see options (conservative vs aggressive) so we can choose trade-offs.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of ML Platform
Veridian AI

Attachments: veridian-matrix-reqs.xlsx

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@veridian.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Capacity lead times & MAP for Dedicated/Private

Alex — great to hear, and thanks for the profile sheet. Draft MAP below; attaching a one-page PDF and a sizing workbook for your procurement team. High-level plan (two options):

1) Evaluation & Staging (2–4 wks)
   - Week 0: Provision short-lived Hosted testbed (no reservation) for integration + smoke tests.
   - Week 1–2: Performance eval (latency P95 targets, throughput tests at 50% and 100% traffic).
   - End of Week 2: Acceptance checkpoint. If pass -> proceed to staging reservation.

2) Reservation path (choose one at checkpoint):
   Option A (Conservative) — 12-week procurement runway + 20% buffer
     - Hardware: Start with 6 H100 (dense inference) or equivalent A100 configuration.
     - Lead time: H100 reserved capacity typical lead-time 10–12 weeks; A100 6–8 weeks depending on region.
     - Buffer: Add 20% headroom for traffic spikes and on-call tolerances.

   Option B (Aggressive) — 6–8 week runway with prioritized tranches
     - Hardware: 4 H100 + burst capacity on Hosted for alpha traffic.
     - Lead time: commit to first tranche (4–6 weeks), second tranche in 8–12 weeks.

Acceptance criteria for reservation sign-off:
- Production P95 latency <= target from your matrix under expected load (we'll run a 1-hour soak at target QPS).
- Token cost within agreed threshold (±10% of estimate).
- Security/compliance items: SOC2 evidence & private VPC network test passed.

Fallback & mitigation:
- If hardware delivery slips, Redwood will temporarily route traffic to Hosted Dedicated pools (region-per-policy) and apply rate-based graceful degradation.
- Fallback pricing and a short-term bridge commitment will be documented in the MAP.

Action items for this week:
- Hannah (me): finalize MAP PDF and capacity workbook (attached) — ready EOD Monday.
- Karthik: provide granular pool sizing & cost delta for A100 vs H100 options.
- Rishi: confirm SOC2 & audit log export timeline for Private deployment.
- Alex/Procurement: confirm target decision date range and internal PO cadence.

I've attached: draft_map_v2.pdf and capacity_estimates_v1.xlsx and linked a working Drive doc (shared). If you want, we can schedule a 30-min runbook session Tues to walk the acceptance tests.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
